questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Living in California, opportunity to study at a renowned university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UC Irvine are great at providing assistance and information, and the international team is very quick to respond to any inquiries. Much better than UCPH.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were events that assisted both in making friends and in formalities. I had no issues whatsoever with getting set up and ready for studying over there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is a private company called American Campus Communities that provides on campus housing. They provide nice amenities such as, swimming pools, game rooms, laundry facilities, study rooms, fitness rooms and more right next to your room. Private rooms in shared apartments are available, but they are expensive. I shared my bedroom with one other person in a shared apartment for 4 in total. I had a good experience with this, but of course there is a risk involved in choosing to share one's bedroom with another. There are also other on campus housing opportunities, but they all resemble the one I had, except for one housing community called Arroyo Vista, which provides more communal living facilities with shared kitchen and bathroom facilities.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: All on campus housing offers cooking facilities. I had a full kitchen that I shared with my three house mates. Meal plans are also available, although I would not recommend buying a meal plan as it is a bit expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The main important piece of information is to know the difference between Arroyo Vista housing and all other on campus communities, as Arroyo Vista is more social but less comfortable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with my housing arrangement, but beware of housing prices in California in general as they are much higher than Copenhagen. Also, if you want a somewhat decent housing rate, be prepared to share your bedroom with another person (you will be able to look for a person that shares your habits and preferences).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a system called webreg, which they will tell you about, it is not complicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: International Center is there for you to answer all the questions you may have.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted except one. For some courses they require specific merits, of which some can be certain basic 1st year courses that you have not taken (ex. basic level academic writing) and they are not flexible with these requirements, so be aware this may make it difficult for you to register for a class that you should be considered fit to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be on the lookout for registration requirements.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The uni offers a wide variety of courses and it is easy to find courses that are of interest to you.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was there as a masters student, but I could only take bachelor level courses because of the exchange agreement. Hence, the courses were much easier than they would have been in UCPH. Bachelor level courses in UC are also a lot easier than bachelor level courses in UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More interaction with the professors, the professors had more freedom in designing their own classes and style of teaching. More tests throughout the course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
UC Irvine has quarter structure, so I took three quarters, corresponding to two semesters. 
In my first quarter I took: Liberalism & Conservatism, Political Participation, and Just War: Revisited.
My second quarter: Modern Political Theory, Capitalism and its Critics, and Enlightenment Legacy.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Third quarter: Justice, American Political Thought, Feminist Political Theory.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any course with prof. Steven Bilakovics or prof. Daniel Brunstetter.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There are some fees that the uni needs you to pay. For each course you take they charge you an administration fee of a few dollars. They also charge you to give you your official transcript after completing your exchange.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is more expensive than you think, especially groceries and housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many clubs do events in everything you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surfing! Visiting LA! Doing road trips to national parks!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See above. Go out in Newport Beach.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It will come naturally, don't worry.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans are welcoming and the other exchange students are also looking for friends, so don't worry.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Americans are so much more open toward strangers, and they are more willing to go out and do stuff together.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is worth all the administrative trouble!
It won't be summer temperatures all year round.
There is no life in Irvine, but don't worry, you will have plenty of things to do around the area once you get settled.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Transportation may seem hopeless in the US without a car, but you will find ways to get around, even if you don't buy a car.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making great new friends and living the California lifestyle.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To remain in contact with friends and family at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
